extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners, patent practitioners, and patent applicants
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural requirements for filing, classifying, and preserving priority/benefit for U.S. patent applications (utility, plant, and design), including provisional applications, international applications designating the U.S., and incorporation-by-reference for inadvertently omitted material under 37 CFR 1.57(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of patent applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent applications can be directed to three broad types of subject matter: (A) applications under 35 U.S.C. 101 for "new and useful process, machine, manufacture, or composition of matter" (utility), (B) plant patents under 35 U.S.C. 161, and (C) design patents under 35 U.S.C. 171.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design and plant applications have specialized procedures (see MPEP Chapters 1500 and 1600). The term "utility" is often used to contrast with plant or design patent applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents required for a national application (35 U.S.C. 111(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: An application must include a specification as prescribed by section 112, a drawing as prescribed by section 113, and an oath or declaration as prescribed by section 115.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The application shall be accompanied by the fee required by law. The fee, oath or declaration, and one or more claims may be submitted after the filing date within a prescribed period and under conditions (including surcharge). Failure to submit within that period causes abandonment. The filing date is when a specification, with or without claims, is received by the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional application requirements (35 U.S.C. 111(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional application must include a specification as prescribed by section 112(a) and any drawings as prescribed by section 113; a claim is not required in a provisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The filing date of a provisional is the date the specification (with or without claims) is received. Fees can be submitted after filing within prescribed periods; failure results in abandonment. A provisional will be regarded as abandoned 12 months after its filing date if not converted or accorded benefit, and will not be subject to revival after that 12‑month period (subject to 119(e)(3)). Provisional applications are not examined for patentability and are not entitled to priority/benefit to foreign or earlier national applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date rules and PLTIA effect
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing date of an application is the date on which a specification, with or without claims, is received in the USPTO; for design patents the filing date requires the specification including at least one claim and any required drawings (35 U.S.C. 171(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective Dec 18, 2013 (PLTIA), nonprovisional applications (except design) filed on/after that date are no longer required to include at least one claim or any drawings to receive a filing date. A nonprovisional filed under 111(a) on or after Dec 18, 2013, may be filed by reference to a previously filed application (foreign, international, provisional, or nonprovisional) (see 35 U.S.C. 111(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of failing to timely submit fee, oath/declaration, or claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The application must be accompanied by required fees; fee, oath/declaration, and at least one claim may be submitted after filing within a prescribed period and under conditions including payment of a surcharge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon failure to submit these items within the prescribed period, the application is regarded as abandoned (except where relief like revival under section 27 is granted if delay shown unavoidable or unintentional as allowed under older statutes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference to previously filed application under 35 U.S.C. 111(c)
rubrics_metrics.description: A nonprovisional application may, under conditions prescribed by the Director, be filed by reference to a previously filed application (specifying application number and intellectual property authority), such that the reference shall constitute the specification and any drawings of the subsequent application for purposes of a filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A copy of the specification and any drawings of the previously filed application must be submitted within such period and under such conditions as prescribed by the Director. Failure to submit the copy within the prescribed period results in the application being regarded as abandoned and treated as never filed unless revived under section 27 and the copy submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of national, provisional, nonprovisional, international, and international design applications (37 CFR 1.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.9 defines: national application (U.S. application filed under 35 U.S.C. 111, certain international applications meeting fee/copy requirements, or international design applications designating the U.S.), provisional application (filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(b)), nonprovisional application, international application (PCT) prior to national processing, and international design application (Hague).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand which regulatory regime applies (national vs national-stage PCT vs international design) because practices differ (e.g., restriction vs unity of invention; notification practices for incomplete applications).

rubrics_metrics.name: Key differences between provisional and nonprovisional applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Significant differences include: (A) No claim is required in a provisional application; (B) No oath or declaration is required; (C) Provisional applications will not be examined for patentability; (D) A provisional application is not entitled to claim priority to any foreign application or benefit of any earlier national application; (E) A design patent application is not entitled to the benefit of a provisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 201.04 for detailed information regarding provisional applications. Provisional apps have limited statutory entitlements compared to nonprovisional apps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion of provisional application to nonprovisional (37 CFR 1.53(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional application filed under paragraph (c) may be converted to a nonprovisional application and accorded the original filing date of the provisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conversion requires the processing fee, must be filed prior to abandonment/payment of issue fee/expiration of 12 months, must include at least one claim as prescribed by 35 U.S.C. 112(b) (unless provisional already contains one), and must include filing, search, and examination fees for the nonprovisional plus any surcharge if basic filing fee or oath/declaration absent on the original filing date. Conversion may adversely affect patent term (term of any patent issuing measured from at least the filing date of the provisional resulting from conversion); applicants are advised to consider claiming benefit under 35 U.S.C. 119(e) instead to avoid adverse patent term impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listing requirement for provisional applications filed on/after July 1, 2022
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional application disclosing nucleotide and/or amino acid sequences is not required to include a separate sequence listing; however, if submitted in a provisional application filed on or after July 1, 2022, any submission of nucleotide and/or amino acid sequence data must be by way of a "Sequence Listing XML" in compliance with §§ 1.831 through 1.834.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comply with XML format requirements for sequence listings to avoid processing issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of an international application designating the United States (35 U.S.C. 363)
rubrics_metrics.description: An international (PCT) application designating the United States shall have the effect, from its international filing date under Article 11 of the Treaty, of a national application for patent regularly filed in the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treatment of national applications under 35 U.S.C. 111 and national-stage applications is similar but not identical; see MPEP §§ 1893.03 et seq. for national-stage examination and § 1896 for differences (e.g., restriction vs unity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and scope of 37 CFR 1.57(b) (incorporation by reference for inadvertently omitted material)
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.57(b) provides that if all or a portion of the specification or drawings were inadvertently omitted from an application, and the application contains a claim for priority/benefit that was present on the filing date, and the omitted portion is completely contained in a prior-filed application, the claim for priority/benefit shall be considered an incorporation by reference of the prior-filed application as to the omitted portion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule is a safeguard allowing inadvertently omitted material to be added by amendment if conditions are met. It does not require an express incorporation-by-reference statement in the later application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions and requirements for adding omitted material under 37 CFR 1.57(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: To add omitted material under 37 CFR 1.57(b) the following must be met: (A) application filed on or after Sept 21, 2004; (B) the specification or drawings were inadvertently omitted; (C) a claim under 37 CFR 1.55 (foreign priority) or 1.78 (benefit) was present on the filing date; (D) the omitted portion must be completely contained in the prior-filed application; (E) applicant must file an amendment to include the omitted portion within any Office-set time, but no later than close of prosecution as defined by 37 CFR 1.114(b) or abandonment; (F) if the application is not otherwise entitled to a filing date, applicant must file a petition under 37 CFR 1.53(e); (G) applicant must supply a copy of the prior-filed application (except where the prior-filed application is filed under 35 U.S.C. 111); (H) applicant must supply an English translation of any non-English prior-filed application; and (I) applicant must identify where the omitted portion can be found in the prior-filed application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All conditions are required; failure of any may render the amendment noncompliant. Where OPAP issues a Notice of Omitted Item(s), respond within the time set (commonly two months) and identify the amendment as under 37 CFR 1.57(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of "completely contained" for 37 CFR 1.57(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Completely contained" requires that the material to be added must be expressly, as opposed to implicitly, disclosed in the prior-filed application as filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The material must be present in the prior-filed application as filed (no reliance on later amendments to the prior application).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on amendments to provisional applications after filing
rubrics_metrics.description: No amendment, other than to make the provisional application comply with the patent statute and regulations, may be made to the provisional application after its filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If conversion or other actions are taken, follow the specific rules for conversion and fees; avoid relying on post‑filing changes to the provisional to supply new matter for priority purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures when prosecution is closed or application is abandoned (adding omitted material)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the prosecution is closed (e.g., final Office action or notice of allowance) or the application is abandoned, applicant may need to reopen prosecution (e.g., file an RCE under 37 CFR 1.114) and/or file petitions to revive under 37 CFR 1.137 to restore pending status in order to add inadvertently omitted material under 37 CFR 1.57(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If material is added by amendment after final action, it has no right of entry and may be treated as an after‑final amendment subject to advisory action. If a patent has issued, adding omitted material via 1.57(b) is not available — consider certificate of correction or reissue (but those cannot be used to add new matter to an issued patent via 1.57(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: International and international design application limitations when using 37 CFR 1.57(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any amendment to an international application pursuant to 37 CFR 1.57(b)(1) is effective only as to the United States and has no effect on the international filing date of the application. For international design applications, amendments under 1.57(b) are effective only as to the U.S. and will not affect the filing date; such amendments will not be acted on prior to entry of the national stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporation-by-reference relief under 1.57(b) cannot be used to alter international filing dates or to accord an international application a filing date under PCT Article 11 if it is otherwise not entitled thereto.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemplar examiner guidance and form paragraphs for noncompliance with 37 CFR 1.57(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners should use form paragraph 6.19.02 to notify applicants that an amendment to add inadvertently omitted material pursuant to 37 CFR 1.57(b) is not in compliance, stating the date and the reason. If the amendment introduces new matter into the disclosure, form paragraph 7.28 must be used; if it adds new matter to the claims or affects the claims, form paragraph 7.31.01 must also be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the amendment is an after-final amendment, an advisory action should indicate that the amendment raises new issues because it is not in compliance with 1.57(b). Do not use the form paragraph where there is an express incorporation by reference (applicant would not need to comply with 1.57(b)).
